=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel — buyer-side review

**Overall recommendation: do not accept the Seller’s package as drafted.** The priority is to protect the AUD 24 million debt-free/cash-free bargain, secure the Bluefen and Riverlark completion deliverables, and prevent broad limitations and disclosure from neutralising specific protections.

The positions below are buyer negotiating recommendations, not assertions that the Seller’s terms are universally outside market. The review is based on the Seller’s summary and Disclosure Letter; the complete SPA and underlying DD documents should be checked before settling the drafting.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the Buyer should want | Recommendation and reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General warranty claims capped at **20% of price: AUD 4.8 million**. | A higher negotiated cap, preferably **100% of price**, or a commercially agreed lower general cap with separate, higher protection for fundamental and identified risks. | **Counter.** A general cap may be negotiable, but AUD 4.8 million can leave significant value impairment unrecoverable. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000** and aggregate claims must exceed **AUD 250,000**; only the excess is recoverable. | Lower thresholds, aggregation of related claims, and a **tipping basket** under which the whole qualifying amount is recoverable once the basket is crossed; exclude specified indemnities and fundamental claims. | **Counter.** The deductible basket and per-claim threshold shift accumulated losses to the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | General warranty claims must be notified within **18 months after Completion**; limitations apply to all claims unless expressly excepted. | At least **24 months** for general warranties, with longer, separately negotiated periods for tax, title and other identified risks; timely notice should preserve a claim through resolution. | **Counter.** Eighteen months may expire before problems emerge, and the blanket application threatens longer-tail claims. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties have the same cap and time limit as general warranties. | Separate fundamental warranties, including capacity, authority, ownership and unencumbered title, with a cap of at least **100% of price**, a materially longer period and no general thresholds. | **Reject.** Failure to acquire good title to the entire company is a fundamental transaction risk, not an ordinary warranty risk. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to **all claims of any nature**, with no stated fraud exception. | Expressly preserve remedies for **fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation and fraudulent concealment**, overriding caps, thresholds, time limits, disclosure, knowledge, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions to the extent legally permissible. | **Reject blanket wording.** It could be argued to restrict recourse for deliberate deception. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the entire indexed data room, accounts, registers and public records; specific disclosures are supplemented by that general disclosure. | Only matters **fairly and specifically disclosed** with sufficient detail to identify their nature and scope should qualify relevant warranties; identify the precise documents and passages. | **Reject blanket disclosure.** A document dump should not transfer unidentified risks to the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by the Buyer or advisers, including anything discoverable in the data room or public records. | Delete constructive and imputed knowledge exclusions; if a limited actual-knowledge qualification is negotiated, define named individuals and actual awareness narrowly, and preserve specific indemnities and fraud claims. | **Reject as drafted.** “Discoverable” could defeat claims regardless of whether the Buyer understood the risk. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied when written consent is delivered, although DD-002 identifies associated conditions and no final consent or satisfaction evidence is included. | A completion condition requiring a valid written change-control consent **and satisfaction or waiver of all applicable conditions**, in form acceptable to the Buyer; provide evidence before Completion and a termination right if not satisfied by the long-stop date. | **Strengthen.** Consent alone may not preserve a customer representing approximately **30% of FY26 revenue**. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2 million** remains outstanding; release to follow Completion. | Repayment from Seller proceeds **at Completion**, supported by an agreed payoff statement and irrevocable discharge/release arrangements for all relevant security, with completion deliverables and a debt-free price adjustment if necessary. | **Reject post-Completion release alone.** The Buyer should not pay a debt-free price while financing and security remain outstanding. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** of conditional Completion bonuses omitted from funds flow; Seller says they are its matter. Payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs are unconfirmed. | Identify beneficiaries, vesting and on-costs; make the Seller bear the bonuses and applicable on-costs through an explicit funds-flow deduction/payment or an equivalent debt-like adjustment, without double counting. | **Amend funds flow and price mechanics.** An unitemised Seller obligation can otherwise become a post-Completion Company cost. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; DD-010 shows **AUD 180,000 open**, but non-payment is not independently verified and no receipt or confirmatory assignment is provided. | Verify payment and obtain evidence of cleared payment plus a confirmatory assignment or other satisfactory title evidence; broaden the indemnity to resulting IP ownership, infringement, remediation and related losses, with a suitable separate regime. | **Expand and verify.** Paying a fee alone may not compensate the Buyer if ownership or use of project materials is challenged. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Characterised as preliminary and not expected to be material; access, scope and notification requirements remain unresolved. | Require an updated investigation, preservation of evidence, scope/access and notification assessment, remediation plan and cooperation; seek a specific indemnity for pre-Completion incident-related losses with appropriate survival and exceptions. | **Do not dismiss or assume a confirmed breach.** The potential exposure involving approximately **1,240 records** is unresolved. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals totalling **AUD 330,000** characterised as ordinary-course costs; the disclosure does not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued. | Review DD-008 and DD-011 together and confirm timing, scope, termination rights and accrual; allocate any pre-Completion or non-ordinary-course obligation through the agreed price mechanics or a specific protection, without double counting. | **Investigate before allocation.** The existing record does not establish that all three are ordinary-course Buyer costs. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Limitations and remedies apply to all claims unless expressly stated otherwise. | Separate regimes for general warranties, fundamental warranties, tax covenant/warranties, specific indemnities, purchase-price adjustments and other contractual claims; state expressly which cap, threshold, time limit and remedy applies to each. | **Redraft the hierarchy.** A broad catch-all can unintentionally undermine protections negotiated for distinct risks. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | DD-012 share register records Harbourglass as holder of **100%**; Seller relies on it as evidence. | Independently verify the register against incorporation and share-issue records, transfers and relevant security searches; obtain completion transfers, register updates, releases and fundamental title warranties. | **Verify before Completion.** The register is important evidence but does not, by itself, resolve every authority, transfer or encumbrance issue. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranties are treated as settled under the general cap and time regime. | Reopen them: seek a **specific pre-Completion tax covenant**, tax warranties with a longer period aligned to relevant assessment periods, and substantive IP ownership/use warranties; give each an appropriate separate liability regime. | **Reopen.** Tax and IP risks can surface later and may not be adequately protected by the general warranty package. |

**Other DD points:** DD-007 indicates a lease **notification**, not an established consent requirement; confirm and satisfy it. DD-009 restricts assignment but does **not** establish that Mossvale consent is required merely for the share sale; review the complete contract before imposing a consent condition.
